mainTopic: May a groom have first relations with his בתולה bride on שבת? The גמרא works through the חתן's exemption from קריאת שמע, a dispute of תנאים, and רבי שמעון's rule of דבר שאין מתכוין.
overview: The גמרא asks whether a groom may have first relations with his בתולה bride on שבת, even though there may be bleeding. רבא reads the ברייתא about 'four nights until מוצאי שבת' as speaking of a groom who already had relations. On that reading it teaches, like שמואל's narrow opening, that later relations are allowed on שבת. רב יוסף objects from the משנה that a חתן is פטור from קריאת שמע through שבת. אביי answers that the exemption comes from the groom's worry, but רבא shows that worry alone does not exempt anyone, since even an אבל is חייב in all the מצוות. רבא then says the question is a dispute of תנאים, shown by two ברייתות about the third night. The same dispute appears openly in another ברייתא, where the חכמים permit first relations on שבת. רבה explains that the חכמים follow רבי שמעון's rule of דבר שאין מתכוין. He adds that this is not פסיק רישיה, because most men are skilled enough to avoid bleeding, and the groomsmen and sheet only guard against hiding blood. Finally, רבי אמי begins a new challenge from a משנה about draining an abscess on שבת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof that first relations are allowed on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא as saying that a groom who has not yet had relations may do so even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the ברייתא saying that if he has not yet had relations with her, he may do so even on שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from the ברייתא it just quoted. It reads the ברייתא as allowing first relations with a בתולה even on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether first relations, which may cause bleeding, are allowed on שבת. The ברייתא says 'he may have relations even on שבת.' The גמרא assumes this means a groom who has not yet had relations at all, which would be a clear היתר.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it? (opens a suggested reading of a source)
had relations (here, the first relations with a בתולה)

phrases.english: What, is it not that if he did not yet have relations,
he may have relations even on שבת?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא quoted just before this section.
steps.raayaObject: First relations with a בתולה are permitted on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that says 'even on שבת' and counts four nights until מוצאי שבת.

steps.title: רבא: The ברייתא means every day except שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the proof and says the ברייתא only allows it on days other than שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: No. The ברייתא means any day except שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the proof. He says the ברייתא does not include שבת at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא only allows relations on weekdays, it says nothing about שבת. The proof from step 1 would then fall away.

phrases.english: Rava said: No, it means except for שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that the ברייתא permits relations on שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא could be talking only about weekdays.

steps.title: אביי: But the four nights include שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that the ברייתא counts four nights until מוצאי שבת, so שבת must be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But the ברייתא says 'until מוצאי שבת, four nights'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's answer straight from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting four nights from Wednesday night until מוצאי שבת must include Friday night, which is שבת. So רבא cannot say the ברייתא leaves out שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: But doesn't it teach…? (a challenge from the wording of a source)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא ״עַד מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת אַרְבָּעָה לֵילוֹת״ קָתָנֵי?
phrases.english: But doesn't it teach, 'until the end of שבת, four nights'?
phrases.notes: Count from Wednesday night: Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and מוצאי שבת. Friday night is שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא עַד מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת אַרְבָּעָה לֵילוֹת קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the ברייתא excludes שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's own count of four nights only works if שבת is included.

steps.title: רבא: The ברייתא is about a groom who already had relations
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new answer. The ברייתא is about a groom who already had first relations before שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It is talking about a case where he already had relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops his first answer and gives a new one. Now שבת is included, but the case is a groom who already had first relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first relations already happened before שבת, there is no concern about first-time bleeding on שבת. So the ברייתא proves nothing about first relations on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer for a new one)

steps.confusionAlert: Both answers here come from רבא. He is not arguing with himself. He replaces his first answer because of אביי's challenge.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: It is where he already had relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's answer from step 2, which אביי knocked down in step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about a groom who has not yet had relations, or it excludes שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא includes שבת but is about a groom who already had first relations.

steps.title: Then what does the ברייתא teach us?
steps.stepSummary: If he already had relations, the גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to tell us anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he already had relations, what is the ברייתא teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's new reading. Relations after the first time seem plainly allowed, so the ברייתא seems to teach nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A source should not say something obvious. So רבא must show what new point the ברייתא is making.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (the statement seems obvious)

phrases.aramaic: אִי כְּשֶׁבָּעַל, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן?
phrases.english: If it is where he already had relations, what is it teaching us?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּשֶׁבָּעַל, מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that the groom already had relations.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On that reading, the ברייתא's statement seems obvious and unnecessary.

steps.title: It teaches that relations are allowed on שבת, like שמואל's narrow opening
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that relations are allowed on שבת even if some blood may come out. This follows שמואל, who allows squeezing through a narrow gap on שבת even though pebbles fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us that one may have relations on שבת, like שמואל. שמואל said: one may enter a narrow opening on שבת, even though he knocks loose pebbles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא does teach something new. Relations on שבת are permitted even after the first time, when there might still be some bleeding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל allows something that is done for a permitted purpose, even if it causes an unintended side effect, like pebbles falling. In the same way, relations are permitted even though some blood may come out. That bleeding is just a side effect, not the goal.

keyTerms.meaning: a narrow gap in a wall

steps.whatToRemember: Bottom line of the first proof: according to רבא's final reading, the ברייתא is about a groom who already had relations. It teaches, like שמואל, that relations are allowed on שבת despite possible bleeding. It does not prove that first relations are allowed on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דִּשְׁרֵי לְמִיבְעַל בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: It teaches us that it is permitted to have relations on שבת,
like Shmuel. As Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: פִּירְצָה דְּחוּקָה מוּתָּר לִיכָּנֵס בָּהּ בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: A narrow opening, one may enter it on שבת,
even though he knocks pebbles loose.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דִּשְׁרֵי לְמִיבְעַל בְּשַׁבָּת, כְּדִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the source has a new point (חידוש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Relations after the first time are so obvious that the ברייתא would not need to say them.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a real חידוש that relations are allowed on שבת despite possible bleeding, like שמואל's narrow opening.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The חתן is exempt from שמע through שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings the משנה that a חתן is פטור from קריאת שמע until מוצאי שבת if he has not yet had relations. He argues this is because he plans to have relations, even on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף raised a source: A groom is exempt from קריאת שמע from the first night until מוצאי שבת, if he has not done the act. Isn't it because he is busy with wanting to have relations?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a new source to prove that first relations are allowed on שבת. The groom's exemption lasts through שבת, which suggests he may have relations then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חתן is exempt because he is focused on doing the first relations, and the exemption runs through שבת, then he must be allowed to do them on שבת. Otherwise there would be no reason to exempt him on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: did the act (had the first relations)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised a source:

phrases.aramaic: חָתָן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיַּת שְׁמַע לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן
phrases.english: A groom is exempt from קריאת שמע on the first night

phrases.aramaic: עַד מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת אִם לֹא עָשָׂה מַעֲשֶׂה.
phrases.english: until the end of שבת, if he has not done the act.
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in ברכות (16a). The wedding of a בתולה was on Wednesday night.

phrases.english: Isn't it because he is preoccupied, since he wants to have relations!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב יוֹסֵף: חָתָן פָּטוּר מִקְּרִיַּת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רבא's reading in steps 4 and 6 (which implies first relations on שבת are forbidden) by bringing a משנה that seems to permit them.
steps.raayaObject: First relations with a בתולה are permitted on שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ברכות exempting a חתן from קריאת שמע until מוצאי שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's position that the ברייתא is only about a groom who already had relations, implying first relations on שבת are forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חתן's exemption from קריאת שמע runs through שבת because he is busy wanting to have relations. That only makes sense if first relations are allowed on שבת.

steps.title: אביי: He is worried because he has not yet done it
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the חתן is exempt because he is anxious that he has not yet had relations. That does not mean he plans to have them on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: No. He is preoccupied because he has not had relations.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רב יוסף's proof. He offers a different reason for the exemption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, the groom's worry about not having done it yet is what exempts him. That worry exists on שבת too, even if he is not allowed to act then. So the exemption on שבת proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: that he has not had relations

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לָא, דִּטְרִיד דְּלָא בְּעֵיל.
phrases.english: Abaye said to him: No, he is preoccupied because he has not had relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לָא, דִּטְרִיד דְּלָא בְּעֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's proof from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that the exemption on שבת shows relations are allowed then.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The exemption could come from worry over not having done it yet, not from a plan to do it on שבת.

steps.title: רבא: Does worry alone exempt a person?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי. If worry alone exempts, then someone whose ship sank should also be exempt from קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Is someone exempt just because he is worried? If so, someone whose ship sank at sea would also be exempt?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's explanation. Ordinary worry cannot be a reason to exempt someone from קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's reason would mean that any upset person is exempt, like a man whose ship just sank. That seems unreasonable. So רבא suggests the חתן's exemption cannot be based on mere worry.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then… (pushing an idea to an extreme result)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וּמִשּׁוּם טִירְדָּא פָּטוּר?
phrases.english: Rava said to him: And is one exempt because of preoccupation?
If so, one whose ship sank at sea,
would he also be exempt?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: וּמִשּׁוּם טִירְדָּא פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's reason given in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the חתן is exempt because of worry.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio: if worry exempts, then anyone upset, like a man whose ship sank, would be exempt.

steps.title: Even an אבל is חייב in all the מצוות except תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the reply 'yes, he would be exempt.' It quotes רב, who says an אבל is חייב in every מצוה except תפילין, because תפילין are called 'פאר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say, 'Yes, he is exempt,' didn't רבי אבא בר זבדא say in the name of רב: An אבל is obligated in all the מצוות stated in the תורה except תפילין, because they are called 'splendor'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens רבא's challenge so that אביי cannot just accept the ship case. Even an אבל, who is surely upset, is still obligated in the מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אבל is in deep pain, yet he is only exempt from תפילין. The reason is not his pain. It is that תפילין are 'splendor,' which does not fit mourning. So worry by itself cannot exempt the חתן, and אביי's explanation is in trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say… (blocking a possible reply)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that being upset does not, on its own, free a person from מצוות. Any exemption needs a special reason.

phrases.english: And if you would say, yes, that is so,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: but didn't Rabbi Abba bar Zavda say in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: אָבֵל חַיָּיב בְּכׇל הַמִּצְוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בְּתוֹרָהּ
phrases.english: A mourner is obligated in all the מצוות stated in the Torah
except for תפילין, since 'splendor' is said about them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכִי נָמֵי — וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר זַבְדָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reinforces רבא's challenge from step 9 by closing off the reply 'yes, he is exempt.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible reply that someone whose ship sank really is exempt because of worry.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אבל, who is clearly upset, is still obligated in all the מצוות except תפילין, so worry alone cannot exempt anyone.

steps.title: רבא: This is a dispute between two ברייתות
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the question of first relations on שבת is a dispute of תנאים. He proves it from two ברייתות that disagree about the חתן on the third night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It is a dispute of תנאים. One ברייתא teaches: if he did not consummate the marriage on the first night, he is פטור on the second night too. If he did not do so on the second night, he is פטור on the third night too. Another ברייתא teaches: on the first and second nights he is פטור, but on the third night he is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the attempt to settle the question from the חתן's worry. Instead he says the question of relations on שבת is simply a dispute between תנאים, and he brings two ברייתות to show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third night is Friday night. The first ברייתא still exempts the חתן then, which suggests he may have relations on שבת. The second ברייתא obligates him on the third night, which suggests first relations on שבת are forbidden, so there is nothing for him to be busy with.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים, the sages of the משנה era
Took action. Here it means he consummated the marriage.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count the nights from שבת. Count them from the wedding. The third night after the wedding is Friday night, and that is why it matters for שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is a dispute of Tannaim.
As one [Baraita] taught:
If he did not take action on the first [night]
phrases.notes: "Take action" means he did not yet have relations with his new wife.

phrases.english: he is exempt even on the second;
[if not] on the second, he is exempt even on the third.
phrases.notes: The third night is Friday night, so this ברייתא exempts him even on שבת.

phrases.english: And another [Baraita] taught:
First and second [nights]: exempt;
third: obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenges in steps 9 and 10, רבא gives up on proving the halacha from the חתן's worry. He says it is a dispute of תנאים instead.
steps.raayaObject: First relations with a בתולה on שבת is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Two ברייתות that disagree about whether the חתן is פטור from קריאת שמע on the third night, which is Friday night.

steps.title: אביי: The ברייתות only disagree about worry
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the two ברייתות may not be arguing about שבת at all. They may disagree only about whether worry over not yet having relations exempts the חתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would אביי answer? There too, they disagree about worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how אביי would answer רבא's proof. It answers that the two ברייתות disagree only about whether the חתן's worry exempts him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's reading, everyone may agree that first relations on שבת are forbidden. The first ברייתא holds that worry about not yet having had relations still exempts him on Friday night. The second holds it does not. So the ברייתות prove nothing about relations on שבת.

phrases.english: And Abaye [how would he answer]?
There too, they disagree about worry.
phrases.notes: This is the same worry אביי used back in step 8 to explain the חתן's exemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רבא's proof from the two ברייתות in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the two ברייתות disagree about relations on שבת.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתות can be read as disagreeing only about whether worry exempts the חתן, not about whether relations on שבת are allowed.

steps.title: The same dispute appears in another ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links the two ברייתות to a third ברייתא. There, one תנא forbids first relations with a בתולה on שבת and the חכמים permit them.
steps.simpleTranslation: These תנאים are like those תנאים. As it was taught: one who marries a בתולה may not have relations for the first time on שבת, and the חכמים permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the dispute between the two ברייתות matches a ברייתא where the question is stated openly. A תנא forbids first relations on שבת, and the חכמים allow them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This backs up רבא's reading. The question of first relations on שבת really is argued directly by תנאים. The ברייתא states the dispute in plain words, without needing to work it out from the rules of קריאת שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: Like these other תנאים. Their dispute matches.

steps.whatToRemember: Whether first relations with a בתולה are allowed on שבת is an open dispute between תנאים. One view forbids it and the חכמים permit it.

phrases.english: And these Tannaim are like those Tannaim.
phrases.notes: The first "these" means the two ברייתות from step 11. The second means the תנאים in the ברייתא about to be quoted.

phrases.english: As it was taught:
One who marries a virgin
may not have relations for the first time on Shabbat,
and the Rabbis permit [it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the dispute between the two ברייתות in step 11 to a ברייתא that states the dispute openly.
steps.raayaObject: First relations on שבת is directly argued by תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where one תנא forbids first relations with a בתולה on שבת and the חכמים permit them.

steps.title: Who are the חכמים who permit it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא stands behind the חכמים who permit first relations with a בתולה on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who the חכמים in the third ברייתא are, the ones who permit first relations with a בתולה on שבת. This is a setup question for the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems hard to allow this act on שבת, since it usually causes bleeding, which looks like a forbidden wound. The גמרא wants to know what reasoning lets the חכמים permit it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages; here, the ones in the ברייתא who permit first relations on שבת

phrases.english: Who are the Sages?
phrases.notes: He means the חכמים from the ברייתא in step 13 who permit first relations with a בתולה on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the lenient opinion just cited in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא, and which reasoning, stands behind the lenient חכמים.

steps.title: רבה: it follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבה says the חכמים are רבי שמעון, who rules that an act whose forbidden result is not intended is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is רבי שמעון, who says that an act a person does not intend is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that the lenient opinion belongs to רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון holds that a forbidden side effect you do not intend does not make the act forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חתן intends to complete the marriage, not to cause bleeding. According to רבי שמעון, דבר שאין מתכוין is allowed, so any bleeding that happens is not a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: An act whose forbidden result the person does not intend

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is Rabbi Shimon,
who said: An unintended act is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים are רבי שמעון, who permits דבר שאין מתכוין.

steps.title: אביי: רבי שמעון agrees when the result is certain
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that רבי שמעון forbids an act whose forbidden result is certain to happen (פסיק רישיה), and bleeding seems certain here.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's answer. Even רבי שמעון forbids an act when the forbidden result will surely happen, and here the bleeding seems to be sure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's leniency only covers results that might or might not happen. If the bleeding is unavoidable, the act counts as פסיק רישיה, and רבי שמעון himself would forbid it. So רבה's answer seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: An act whose forbidden result is certain to happen

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But doesn't Rabbi Shimon agree
in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
phrases.notes: This is a picture of a result that is certain: if you cut off an animal's head, of course it dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מוֹדֶה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בִּפְסִיק רֵישֵׁיהּ וְלָא יְמוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבה's answer from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the חכמים rely on רבי שמעון's rule of דבר שאין מתכוין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bleeding is a certain result, so the case is פסיק רישיה, which רבי שמעון forbids.

steps.title: Some men are skilled enough to avoid bleeding
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that, unlike the Babylonians, some men are skilled at a careful method that avoids causing bleeding, so it is not certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Not like these Babylonians who are not skilled at turning aside; there are those who are skilled at turning aside.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי. Bleeding is not certain, because some men know how to avoid it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If skilled men can avoid the bleeding, it is no longer a sure result. That removes the case from פסיק רישיה and puts it back under רבי שמעון's leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: Turning aside, a careful method that avoids causing bleeding

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבה is the one answering אביי here.

phrases.english: Not like these Babylonians
who are not skilled at turning aside;
rather, there are those who are skilled at turning aside.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כְּהַלָּלוּ בַּבְלִיִּים שֶׁאֵין בְּקִיאִין בְּהַטָּיָיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the forbidden result is avoidable, not certain.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bleeding is unavoidable, so the case is פסיק רישיה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Skilled men can avoid bleeding, so the case falls under דבר שאין מתכוין.

steps.title: Then why is the חתן worried?
steps.stepSummary: If the חתן can avoid bleeding, why is he worried enough to be exempt from קריאת שמע?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why is he troubled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's answer. If the act can be done without bleeding, the חתן should have nothing to worry about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the חתן was exempt from קריאת שמע because of his worry. If he is skilled and the act carries no risk of a שבת problem, that worry seems to be gone.

phrases.english: If so, why is he troubled?
phrases.notes: This points back to the worry that frees a חתן from קריאת שמע, from step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that the act can be done without bleeding.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the act involves no risk, the חתן has no reason to worry, yet the halacha treats him as worried.

steps.title: The worry is for the unskilled
steps.stepSummary: The worry applies to a חתן who is not skilled.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one who is not skilled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חתן who is exempt because of worry is the one who is not skilled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The skilled man has no worry. The unskilled one does, and he is the one the exemption is speaking about.

phrases.english: For one who is not skilled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: the skilled man is not worried, and the unskilled man is.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every חתן is skilled, so none should be worried.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption for worry is about the unskilled חתן.

steps.title: Then the rule should separate skilled and unskilled
steps.stepSummary: If skill makes the difference, the חכמים should have ruled that the skilled man is permitted and the unskilled man is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them say: one who is skilled is permitted, and one who is not skilled is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. If some men can avoid bleeding and some cannot, the חכמים should have given a split ruling instead of a blanket permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the unskilled man, bleeding is certain, which is פסיק רישיה. So he should be forbidden. The ברייתא, however, permits it without any split.

phrases.english: Let them say: one who is skilled is permitted,
one who is not skilled is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: יֹאמְרוּ: בָּקִי מוּתָּר, שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּקִי אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of step 19 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The blanket permission of the חכמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the unskilled man causes certain bleeding, a blanket permission is too broad.

steps.title: Most men are skilled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that most men are skilled, so the ruling follows the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Most are skilled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that most men are skilled, so the חכמים gave one general ruling of permission.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since most men can avoid the bleeding, the act in general is not a certain cause of bleeding. The ruling follows the usual case and does not stop to split it.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים permit first relations on שבת according to רבי שמעון, because most men can avoid the bleeding, so it is not פסיק רישיה.

phrases.english: Most are skilled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeals to the majority: the general ruling follows most people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Skilled and unskilled are equally common, so a split ruling would be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Most men are skilled, so a general permission is given.

steps.title: Then why groomsmen and a sheet?
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב חנן asks: if most men can avoid bleeding, why are groomsmen and a sheet needed to check the bride's virginity?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב חנן said to אביי: If so, why are there groomsmen? Why is there a sheet?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב חנן challenges the idea that most men are skilled. If so, checking for blood would prove nothing, so why are these checks used?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Groomsmen and a sheet were used to confirm whether the bride was a בתולה, based on the presence of blood. If most men usually avoid bleeding, the lack of blood shows nothing, and these checks seem pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: If that is so (introduces a challenge from what was just said)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא בַּר רַב חָנָן לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Ḥanan said to Abaye:
If that is so, why are there groomsmen?
phrases.notes: The groomsmen were there to make sure nobody played tricks about whether the bride was a בתולה.

phrases.english: Why is there a sheet?
phrases.notes: The sheet was used to show whether there was blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim of step 21 that most men are skilled.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that most men can avoid bleeding.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If bleeding is usually avoided, the lack of blood proves nothing, so groomsmen and a sheet would serve no purpose.

steps.title: The checks guard against hiding the evidence
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the groomsmen and the sheet are there in case the חתן sees blood and tries to destroy that evidence.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, it is in case he sees and destroys it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the checks are not because blood always appears. They are there in case blood does appear and the חתן tries to get rid of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A skilled man can avoid bleeding if he wants to. But when there is bleeding, the groomsmen and the sheet make sure the evidence is not hidden. So the checks still have a purpose.
steps.whatToRemember: Groomsmen and a sheet do not prove that bleeding always happens. They guard against hiding the evidence when it does happen.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: אביי is answering רבא בר רב חנן.

phrases.english: There, it is lest he see and destroy it.
phrases.notes: He means the חתן might see the blood and try to get rid of that evidence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the checks.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The checks exist because blood always appears.
steps.terutzMaskana: The checks exist to stop the חתן from hiding blood when it does appear.

steps.title: רבי אמי challenges from the case of draining an abscess on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי quotes a משנה: one who drains an abscess on שבת to make an opening is חייב, but if he only wants to let out pus, a different ruling follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי raised an objection from a משנה: Someone who drains an abscess on שבת: if he does it to make an opening for it, he is liable. And if he does it to let out the pus from it...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי starts a new attack on the idea that the first בעילה is allowed on שבת. He quotes a משנה about draining an abscess, and the משנה continues past the end of this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה depends on what the person is trying to do. If he wants to make a real opening in the body, he is חייב. The first בעילה also seems to create an opening, so this משנה looks like a challenge to allowing it on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: One who opens or drains a swelling
An abscess, a swelling filled with pus
Literally a mouth; here, a lasting opening
Pus or fluid inside the abscess
Liable, meaning he broke a שבת prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: Do not decide the ruling for removing pus yet. The משנה's second half continues right after this section ends.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami raised an objection:
One who drains an abscess on Shabbat,
if it is to make an opening for it, he is liable.
phrases.notes: He means a lasting opening that stays open, not just a quick poke.

phrases.english: And if it is to let out pus from it —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the blood question was settled with אביי's answer, a new challenge is raised from a different angle: making an opening on שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the first בעילה is allowed on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes a person liable when he drains an abscess in order to create an opening. The first בעילה seems to create an opening too, so it should also be forbidden on שבת.
